_doc: Construction knowledge base for the staged clothing workflow (garment_design.py, cloth_workflow.py). Data, not prose: the design sheet's defaults, the evidence checks that prove a construction choice is really in the pattern, the dimensions a tailor works to, fabrics with physical numbers, and the numeric targets a simulated garment is judged by. Lengths in mm unless a key says otherwise; ease as a fraction of the body girth (flat pattern, seam to seam). Sources: tailoring practice as summarised in cloth_audit.md (2026-10-03), the Marvelous Designer field guide 2024, Threads (shirt collars), Aldrich (skirt, trouser blocks), FreeSewing's design docs. Every lesson of the audit is either a default, an evidence check or a target here; `lessons` says which.

roles._doc: Piece roles. A piece's role is its design-table/piece key "role", else the first alias its name (without .L/.R/.m and digits) matches. Checks address roles, never piece names, so they work on any design.

kinds._doc: Garment kinds. fit: ease bands per girth (fraction of the body girth, from the flat pattern). details: the default choice per detail (garment_design fills these in when the sheet leaves them out). required: details every garment of the kind must state or take by default. cap_ease: the sleeve cap's ease into the armhole. lap: which front laps over at a closure (the buttonhole side is the outer one). sewing_order: roles in the order a maker joins them (the construction plan follows it). region: upper (shoulders carry it), lower (waist carries it), whole.

flat._doc: A flat thing: a tablecloth, a blanket, a curtain (state draped).

details._doc: Per detail kind, the choices. made_of: the pieces (roles) it adds, whether they're interfaced and how they rest (as_made: wholly interfaced pieces rest in their made shape; flat: rest on the flat pattern). seams: [role, role, seam kind]. folds: fold lines (see cloth_guide: angle on the pattern-face side, 180 flat, 0 folded over onto the face, 360 folded under). needs: details this choice can't be made without. dims: what a tailor works to ([lo, hi] mm unless named otherwise). evidence: checks that prove the choice is in the pattern (garment_design.EVIDENCE). lessons: why (and which audit item).

shirt_collar.label: two-piece shirt collar: a stand sewn to the neckline, a turned fall sewn to the stand's top

folds.where: 3 mm above the fall/stand seam (the roll)

lessons: The fall must cover the stand and its neckline seam by 6-10 mm at CB (audit: ours stopped 13 mm above it: a funnel). Checked: dim fall_cover on the pattern, collar_cover after the sim.
The roll is a crease a few mm above the collar/stand seam, not a 10 mm U (the U ate 15.7 mm of the fall). A fold line with angle, not a placement shape.

convertible.label: one-piece convertible collar sewn straight to the neckline (worn open or closed)

folds.where: the roll line, ~25-30 mm up at CB

notched_lapel.label: notched lapel: the fronts turn back along a roll line from the break point to the gorge, faced; a collar with stand from the gorge round the back

folds.where: the roll line: break point (top button) to the roll line's end at the neck

lessons: Interfacing stiffens the fronts but must not freeze them: fronts resting 'as made' (flat on the torso) can't roll (audit fix 1). Checked: not_made front.
Without a facing a rolled lapel shows the wrong side. Checked: piece facing.
The stand is sewn from roll-line end to roll-line end, not CF to CF (it was -23.8%).

shawl.label: shawl collar: the lapel and collar one piece cut on with the front, rolled

hood.label: hood: two sides (or sides + centre panel) sewn round the neckline, the face edge turned or bound

folds.where: the face edge turned in 20-30 mm

rib_neckband.label: rib neckband: a folded rib strip 10-15% shorter than the neckline, stretched on

folds.where: along its middle (folded in half lengthwise)

lessons: A rib band is shorter than the edge it is sewn to: that stretch is what makes it lie flat. A 1:1 band gapes.

bound_neckline.label: bias binding round the neckline (5-8 mm finished)

faced_neckline.label: neckline finished with a facing turned inside (no collar)

none.label: no collar (a raw or hemmed edge)

barrel.label: barrel cuff: a closed band buttoned round the wrist; the sleeve enters through a placket opening, 2-3 pleats folded toward it
lessons: Closed girth = wrist + 25-40 mm; height 60-70 mm (ours 57).
A closed sleeve tube sewn round a cuff whose ends overlap has nowhere to put the overlap: the sleeve needs a placket opening (audit fix 6). Checked through needs: sleeve_placket.

french.label: French cuff: a double-height cuff folded back on itself, closed with links

rib.label: knit rib cuff: a folded rib tube 15-25% smaller than the sleeve end

hemmed.label: no cuff: the sleeve end turned up and stitched

elastic.label: elastic casing at the sleeve end

tower.label: tower placket: a slit 120-150 mm on the little-finger side, an underlap binding and a pointed overlap placket
lessons: Simon drafts the sleevePlacketUnderlap/Overlap and a placketCut line; our design table didn't use them (audit fix 6).

continuous.label: continuous bound placket (a strip binding the slit)

none.label: no placket (sleeve end open or knit)

buttons.label: single-breasted, buttoned through a placket
lessons: The buttonhole side laps over (men's: left over right). Checked: lap.

double_breasted.label: double-breasted: two columns of buttons, the fronts overlapping 90-120 mm

zip.label: zip front (a separating zip between the fronts)

pullover.label: no front opening (pulled over the head)

folded.label: cut-on placket: the front edge folded under twice (button side) / folded to the outside 32-38 mm (buttonhole side), interfaced
lessons: Today the turn op CUTS the fold off (one layer + an interfacing band): the folded layers and their pressed edges aren't modelled. A fold-line primitive (zozo2) will let the placket keep its turns.

separate.label: separate placket strip sewn to the front edge

half.label: half placket (polo): a short opening at CF

straight.label: straight waistband: a folded, interfaced band, 30-40 mm finished, its ends lapped and buttoned

contoured.label: contoured (curved) waistband sitting below the waist

zip_fly.label: zip fly: a fly extension on the left front, a fly shield behind the right

cb_zip.label: centre-back zip 180-220 mm from the waist; the CB seam below it sewn

side_zip.label: zip in the left side seam

welt.label: welt pocket (a slot with a welt, bag inside)

in_seam.label: pocket bag in the side seam (invisible from outside)

kangaroo.label: kangaroo pocket on a hoodie's front

hem._doc: Hems aren't in the seam-line pattern: the hem depth goes to the detail maps (cloth DETAIL hem), and a fold line where the solver can hold it.

shirttail.label: curved shirttail hem, narrow double-turned 5-6 mm, edge-stitched

blind.label: blind-stitched hem 30-50 mm (skirts, trousers), invisible from outside

coat.label: coat hem 40-50 mm turned and blind-stitched (sleeve hems 30-40)

coverstitch.label: knit hem turned 20-25 mm and coverstitched (two parallel rows)

rib_band.label: rib band at the hem (hoodies, sweatshirts)

waist.label: waist darts (skirts, trousers' back): 80-140 mm long, 15-30 mm intake

box_back.label: box pleat at the back below the yoke

lapped_vent.label: lapped vent / pleat at CB: one side's extension (35-50 mm) laps over the other, tacked at the top, NOT sewn full length
lessons: Carlton's tail CB was sewn shut full length: the 36 mm strips lay in the plane (the 'crossings at the vent'). Audit fix 5.

back_belt.label: a half belt between back and tail (Carlton): it closes the gap the side seams need
lessons: Leaving Carlton's belt out made back + tail 83 mm shorter than the front side seam (-20.5% / -5.6%).

edge.label: edge-stitched 1.5-3 mm from collar, stand, cuffs, placket edges

flat_fell.label: flat-felled seams: two rows 6 mm apart on one side

interfacing._doc: Bending multiplier over the shell per stiffening (cloth FABRICS 'stiff' is the solver's multiplier; real fused interfacing is 5-20x the shell's bending).

fabrics._doc: Fabric choices with physical numbers (weight g/m2, thickness mm, stretch: woven or knit, bending length mm = (B/w)^(1/3), the drape scale) and the cloth preset + overrides the solver gets. A 'fabric' in a design sheet is one of these names, or a cloth preset name, or {preset, overrides}.

designs._doc: What each draft source can make: per detail choice, the recipe (FreeSewing options, pieces dropped, fold lines, generated pieces) and what it can't make yet (and why). A sheet choice a design can't make is a hard failure in stage 1. fit_options: draft options per fit. pattern_from: the cloth design table / block name (default: the design's own name).

cannot.sleeve_placket.tower: Simon drafts sleevePlacketUnderlap/Overlap and a placketCut line, but our design table doesn't cut the slit or sew the plackets yet (audit fix 6). Choose "none" and accept the cuff join's -1.8% (it shows as a twisted, ruffled join), or build the slit
cannot.placket.separate: separateButtonPlacket isn't in the design table

cannot.lining.full: the table is the shell only (no lining pieces)
cannot.lining.half: the table is the shell only
cannot.belt.back_belt: carlton.belt is drafted by FreeSewing but not in the table yet (zozo2 is adding it)
cannot.back_vent.lapped_vent: the tail's CB is sewn full length (zozo2 is adding the lapped pleat)
no vent extension in the block yet

targets._doc: Numeric targets a simulated garment is judged by (cloth_audit.md part 3; measured on reference photos). stage: which quality they apply to ('final' = at <= 5-10 mm triangles; 'draft' numbers are reported, not judged). The workflow's sim check reads these.

collar_cover_mm._doc: how far the fall's edge lies below the neckline seam at CB (+ = covers)

hem_level_mm._doc: hem height spread across the front (hung: hem swing) or round the body (a skirt worn)

waistband_at_waist_mm._doc: waistband's median height minus the body's waist line

crest_radius_p10_mm._doc: needs <= 5 mm triangles; at 1 cm the floor is ~7 mm

crease_width_mm._doc: FWHM from renders (audit method); not measured by the tools yet

fold_spacing_mm._doc: not measured by the tools yet

start_strain_over_limit._doc: strain-limited solvers (ZOZO) can't start past their limit: triangles of the start stretched past it against the rest

lessons.lesson: Construction before solver: a day of stiffness/shear/mesh tuning chased symptoms whose cause was the pattern (cap ease 44%, a stretched stand, a missing belt, a pleat sewn shut, no sleeve placket, no lapel roll or facing, nothing pressed, one bend for every fabric).
lessons.where: workflow: dress refuses to simulate while design/pattern checks fail hard (force=True overrides)

lessons.lesson: Sleeve cap ease: shirt 0-3%, coat/jacket 3-6%, knit -3..+3%.
Every seam within +-1.5% unless it is designed to ease; notches aligned within 6 mm.
A notched lapel needs a roll line (fold), a facing and fronts that aren't frozen as made.
A barrel cuff needs a sleeve placket.
The collar fall covers the stand by 6-10 mm at CB.
Layers lie touching (1 mm shirt, 3-4 mm coat): placement offsets of 4-10 mm read padded.
The cloth reads thick below ~7 mm crests at 1 cm triangles: finals at <= 5 mm on visible pieces.
Every fabric its own bend: fabrics carry physical numbers, interfacing its multiplier.
Hems differ by kind: shirttail 6 mm, blind 40 mm, coat 45 mm, none on bagged collar/cuff edges.
Coat buttons are 20-25 mm, shirt 10-12 mm; buttonholes horizontal on cuffs, stands and coats.
lessons.where: details.front_closure dims (maps don't size buttons per design yet)

lessons.lesson: A strain-limited solver can't start past its limit; nothing may start through anything else.
Interfaced pieces resting as made keep their placed shape: fine for a collar or cuff, wrong for anything that must roll (coat fronts).
Sleeves on a hanger hang within ~8 deg of vertical.
